lexicon.lane_en: 1 بُلُوغٌ بلوغ [inf. n. of بَلَغَ ] and إِبْلَاغٌ [inf. n. of , but it seems that ابلاغ is here a mistranscription for بَلَاغٌ , which is, like بُلُوغٌ , an inf. n.

body.meaning_en: to reach, to arrive at, to attain
body.morphology: verbal noun of eloquence, from balagha, 'he reached'; eloquence is speech that reaches its mark
body.semantic_field: spans reaching a place, attaining a goal, conveying a message, and speech that hits home
body.text_en: The root ب-ل-غ is about arriving — reaching a destination or driving a message home to its hearer. Balagha is eloquence understood this way: speech so apt it reaches its aim exactly, which is why Ali's collected words are titled the Nahj al-Balagha, 'the Way of Eloquence.'

lexicon.lane_en: 1 بَشَرَ ذ , aor. بَشُرَ , (S, Msb,) inf. n. بَشْرٌ ; (S, Msb, K;) and , (A,) inf. n. إِبْشَارٌ ; (K;) He pared (S, A, Msb, K) a hide, (S, A, Msb,) removing its بَشَرَة , (S,) or face, or surface, (A, Msb,) or the skin upon which the hair grew: (TA:) or, as some say, removing its inner part with a large knife: or, accord.

body.meaning_en: outer skin; (hence) mankind; glad tidings
body.morphology: A collective noun from the sense of bashara, the outer skin, extended to human beings as skin-clad mortals.
body.semantic_field: links the outer skin and surface to humankind, and separately to the bringing of good news that shows on the face.
body.text_en: The root b-sh-r first means the outer skin, and from it bashar comes to mean humankind — mortals defined by that skin. The same root branches into bushra, glad tidings, because good news is what visibly brightens the skin of the face.

derivatives.meaning_en: a lining; an inner circle of intimates

lexicon.lane_en: بَطْنٌ طن بطن بطنن The belly, or abdomen; i. e. the part of the body which is separated from the جَوْف [i. e. chest, or thorax, ] by the حِجَاب [i. e. midriff, or diaphragm ]; containing the liver and the spleen and the stomach and the lower intestines &c.; (Zj in his “ Khalk el-Insán; ” [in which it is erroneously said to comprise also the lungs;]) contr.

body.meaning_en: belly; the inner, hidden part
body.morphology: An active participle of batana ('to be hidden within'), so al-batin is 'that which is inward' — the concealed meaning under the surface.
body.semantic_field: spans the physical belly and interior and, figuratively, everything hidden, inward and concealed.
body.text_en: The root b-t-n names the belly and, by extension, the inner and hidden part of anything. Al-batin is therefore the concealed inner meaning beneath a text's outward wording — the exact object this book's esoteric interpretation sets out to draw up.

derivatives.meaning_en: a mutual transaction; a pledge of allegiance

body.meaning_en: to sell, to conclude a transaction
body.morphology: A noun of instance (bay'ah) naming a single act of the concluding handclasp of a deal.
body.semantic_field: Spans buying and selling, striking a bargain, and the handshake that seals it.
body.text_en: The root means to sell and seal a transaction with a clasp of hands. A bay'ah borrows that image for the pledge of allegiance — a binding covenant struck like a solemn deal.

body.meaning_en: to limit, define a boundary, sharpen
body.morphology: the plural of ḥadd, 'a limit or edge', used for the fixed legal boundaries and their prescribed penalties
body.semantic_field: the root spans boundaries, edges, sharpness, and definition/restraint
body.text_en: The root ḥ-d-d means to set an edge or boundary, whether a physical limit or a sharpened blade. The ḥudūd are the fixed limits God has set, and by extension the defined penalties for crossing them; the same root names iron (ḥadīd), the sharp and hard metal.

lexicon.lane_en: 1 ذَكَرَهُ ذ , [aor. ذَكُرَ ,] inf. n. ذِكْرَى , (S, A, Msb,) which is fem., (Msb,) and imperfectly decl., (S,) and ذِكْرٌ (A, K) [and ذُكْرٌ , or, accord. to EtTebreezee, (Ham p.

body.meaning_en: to remember, to mention, to recall
body.morphology: verbal noun (maṣdar) of dhakara, 'he remembered / mentioned'
body.semantic_field: spans inward memory, spoken mention, invocation, and reminder
body.text_en: The root ذ-ك-ر carries a single idea across two directions: to hold something in the mind and to speak it aloud. From it, dhikr is the disciplined remembrance of God — both the silent awareness and the repeated invocation of His name.

body.meaning_en: to perish, pass away, cease to be
body.morphology: verbal noun of faniya, 'he / it perished'
body.semantic_field: spans perishing, transience, evanescence, and coming to an end
body.text_en: The root ف-ن-ي marks all that is passing — the Qur'an says everything upon the earth is fānin, bound to perish. In the mystical vocabulary of this book, fana is the willed disappearance of the self, the ego passing away so that only God remains.

body.meaning_en: to explain, expound, uncover
body.morphology: A form-II verbal noun of fassara, the intensive of fasara ('to uncover'), meaning the detailed explaining-out of a text's meaning.
body.semantic_field: concerns uncovering, clarifying and laying open what is obscure.
body.text_en: The root f-s-r means to uncover and lay bare what is hidden in a text. Tafsir is the intensive, detailed form of that uncovering — the outward exegesis of scripture, produced by a mufassir, that this book contrasts with the inner ta'wil.

lexicon.lane_en: غُفْلٌ ذ Land without cultivation: (K:) or without any way-mark: (Msb:) or without any waymark and without cultivation: (S, O:) or not rained upon: (Ks, S, O:) or unknown; in which is no known trace; or vestige: and, accord.

body.meaning_en: to be heedless, unaware, neglectful
body.morphology: noun from ghafala, 'he was heedless / inattentive'
body.semantic_field: spans heedlessness, negligence, and the blank inattention of the unmindful
body.text_en: The root غ-ف-ل describes an untended emptiness — land with no landmark, a mind with no attention. Ghafla is the spiritual form of this: heedless forgetfulness of God, the exact opposite of the wakeful remembrance that dhikr demands.

derivatives.meaning_en: he made a pact with another

body.meaning_en: to pledge, to covenant, to charge with a duty
body.morphology: verbal noun of ʿahida, 'he made a covenant / took a pledge'
body.semantic_field: spans covenant, binding pledge, solemn charge, and the keeping of one's word
body.text_en: The root ع-ه-د is the language of solemn promise — to bind oneself by a pledge and be charged with keeping it. Ahd is that covenant, whether the compact between God and humanity or the charge of office Ali lays on his governor Malik al-Ashtar.

body.meaning_en: to limit, set a boundary, sharpen
body.morphology: Plural of hadd ("limit, boundary"), a noun formed directly from the root.
body.semantic_field: The root covers edges, limits, and definitions — the line that separates one thing from another.
body.text_en: Hudud is the plural of hadd, the boundary or limit that defines where one thing ends and another begins. In this book the word names the ordered ranks of a hierarchy, each rank a defined threshold, drawn from the root's core sense of a fixed edge.

derivatives.meaning_en: those screened off, kept from sight
a doorkeeper; the brow that shields the eye

lexicon.lane_en: حِجَابٌ حاجب حجاب [ A thing that prevents, hinders, debars, or precludes: ] a thing that veils, conceals, hides, covers, or protects; (S, Msb, K TA;) because it prevents seeing, or beholding: (Msb:) a thing, (A, K,) or body.

body.meaning_en: to veil, screen, bar from sight
body.morphology: An instrument-noun form from the root, naming the thing that screens or partitions — a veil or barrier.
body.semantic_field: The root spans covering, concealing, and barring — anything that stands between the eye and what lies beyond it.
body.text_en: Hijab comes from a root meaning 'to veil or bar.' It names whatever screens one thing from another — a curtain, a partition, or a barrier that prevents seeing across it.

body.meaning_en: to aim for, betake oneself; to prove, argue
body.morphology: A noun on the fa'la pattern meaning the decisive proof or authority one 'betakes oneself to' when establishing a claim.
body.semantic_field: runs from purposeful going toward a goal to the argument, evidence or authoritative figure by which a case is won.
body.text_en: The root h-j-j means to set out purposefully toward something, which is why the pilgrimage is called hajj. A hujja is the proof or authority one 'betakes oneself to' to settle a matter — a conclusive argument, or the person who embodies it.

derivatives.meaning_en: an emigrant, one who leaves home
a place of emigration or refuge

body.meaning_en: to abandon, forsake, cut off, emigrate
body.morphology: hijra is a verbal noun of the form-I verb, the act of severing ties with a place and departing from it.
body.semantic_field: spans forsaking, breaking off relations, and migrating away from home.
body.text_en: The root ه-ج-ر means to break away and leave a thing behind, to cut the ties that hold one to a place. The Hijra is the Prophet's emigration from Mecca to Medina, the departure so decisive it became the start of the Muslim calendar.

derivatives.meaning_en: a place, a locus (where one alights)

body.meaning_en: to untie, to loosen, to make permissible
body.morphology: A noun on the fa'al pattern meaning that which has been loosed and so is lawful.
body.semantic_field: Spans untying, alighting/settling, and releasing a thing into permissibility.
body.text_en: The root means to untie or loosen a knot. Halal is what has been loosed from prohibition — an act 'unknotted' and therefore permitted.

body.meaning_en: to forbid; to make sacred and inviolable
body.morphology: A noun on the fa'al pattern meaning that which is prohibited or set apart as inviolable.
body.semantic_field: Spans prohibition, sanctity, and the inviolable — the two joined by the idea of a boundary not to be crossed.
body.text_en: The root joins two ideas under one boundary: to forbid, and to make sacred. Haram is what lies across that line — an act forbidden because a sacred limit has been set around it.

derivatives.meaning_en: a year; a turning; power to act

lexicon.lane_en: 1 حَالَ حال , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. يَحُولُ , Msb, Er-Rághib,) inf. n. حَوْلٌ and حُؤُولٌ (K, Er-Rághib) [and حَوَلَانٌ ], It (a thing) became altered, transmuted, or changed, (S, * Mgh, Msb, Er-Rághib, TA,) from its state, or condition, (S, Mgh,) or from its natural state or condition, and its constitution; as also ; (Msb;) i.

body.meaning_en: to change, turn, transfer
body.morphology: A noun from the root, naming the transfer or turning-over of a debt from one party to another.
body.semantic_field: The root spans changing, turning, and shifting — from a thing altering its state to the turning of a full year (hawl).
body.text_en: Hawala derives from the root meaning 'to change or turn over.' As a commercial term it is the transfer of a debt from one person to another — the obligation is 'turned' from one shoulder to the next.

body.meaning_en: to fall, to incline downward, to crave
body.morphology: noun from hawā, 'he inclined / fell'; names the soul's downward pull
body.semantic_field: runs from physical falling to inclination, craving, and unchecked caprice
body.text_en: The root ه-و-ي is about falling and being pulled downward, and from it comes the abyss itself. Hawa is the soul's gravity — the low craving and caprice that drags a person down, set in this book against the upward pull of the intellect.

body.meaning_en: to strive, to exert effort
body.morphology: A form III verbal noun (mujahadah) meaning sustained struggle, here directed against the self.
body.semantic_field: Spans effort, exertion, and struggle against resistance.
body.text_en: The root means to strain and exert oneself to the limit. Mujahadah is the inner form of that striving — the disciplined struggle against one's own appetites and laziness.

body.meaning_en: to strip, denude, lay bare
body.morphology: A form-II verbal noun of jarrada, the act of stripping something down to nothing but itself.
body.semantic_field: The root spans peeling, baring, and abstraction — removing every covering until only the essence remains.
body.text_en: Tajrid is the act of stripping every attribute away, from a root meaning to denude or lay bare. In the book's argument it is the method of removing all descriptions from the idea of God until nothing composite or added remains.

lexicon.lane_en: خُطْبَةٌ خطب خطبه خطبة , a word of the measure فُعْلَةٌ in the sense of the measure مَفْعُولَةٌ , like نُسْخَةٌ in the sense of مَنْسُوخَةٌ , and غُرْفَةٌ مِنَ المَآءِ in the sense of مَغْرُوفَةٌ ; meaning An exhortation or admonition [ recited by a خَطِيب ] : (Msb:) a form of words, a discourse, a sermon, a speech, an oration, or a harangue, which the خَطِيب recites on the pulpit: (K, * TA:) [in the noon-service of the congregational mosque on Friday, the خطيب recites two forms of words, each of which is thus termed: the former chiefly consists of expressions of praise to God, blessings on …

body.meaning_en: to address, speak formally, court
body.morphology: a fuʿlah-pattern noun in the sense of the passive participle: the formal address that is 'delivered' to an audience
body.semantic_field: the root spans formal speech, addressing an audience, weighty matters, and the courting of marriage
body.text_en: The root kh-ṭ-b centers on addressing others in serious, formal speech. A khuṭbah is the sermon or oration delivered from the pulpit, and the same root gives khiṭāb, formal discourse, and even khaṭb, a grave matter that calls for such address.

lexicon.lane_en: خُلَاصَةُ السَّمْنِ خلاصة السمن (S, A, L, Msb, K) and خِلَاصَتُهُ (Fr, Sgh, K) What has become clear, of cooked butter; (S, A, L, K;) or cooked butter into which some dates have been thrown, or into which some سَوِيق [i.

body.meaning_en: to be pure, clear, unmixed, free of admixture
body.morphology: verbal noun of the form-IV verb akhlaṣa, 'he made pure / sincere'
body.semantic_field: spans purity, clarity, distillation, and being set apart from anything foreign
body.text_en: The root خ-ل-ص describes something refined until nothing foreign remains, like butter clarified to its essence. Ikhlas applies this to intention: a devotion so purified of any motive other than God that it belongs to Him alone.

body.meaning_en: to be pure, clear, and unmixed
body.morphology: A form IV verbal noun (ikhlas) meaning the act of making something purely and exclusively for one end.
body.semantic_field: Spans purity, clearing away, and being freed of admixture.
body.text_en: The root means to be pure and free of anything mixed in. Ikhlas is purifying one's intention so worship is for God alone, with no trace of showing off blended in.

lexicon.lane_en: خِمْسٌ خمس The drinking of camels on the fifth day, counting the day of the next preceding drinking as the first; their drinking one day, then pasturing three days, then coming to the water on the fifth day, the first and last days, on which they drink, being thus reckoned : this is the correct explanation, accord.

body.meaning_en: five; a fifth
body.morphology: a noun (khumus/khums) meaning 'one-fifth', built directly on the number five
body.semantic_field: the root spans the number five and its fractions and multiples
body.text_en: The root kh-m-s is simply the number five and its derived fractions. Khums is the obligatory one-fifth levy, named directly for the fraction it represents.

derivatives.meaning_en: the choice; the best of a thing

lexicon.lane_en: خَيْرٌ خير [ Good, moral or physical; anything that is good, real or ideal, and actual or potential; and, being originally an inf. n., used as sing and pl.;] a thing that all desire; such as intelligence, for instance, and equity; (Er-Rághib, and so in some copies of the K;) [or goodness; ] and excellence; and what is profitable or useful; benefit; (Er-Rághib;) contr.

body.meaning_en: to be good; to choose the better
body.morphology: A verbal noun from the root, naming the exercised right of choosing the better of two options (as in a sale).
body.semantic_field: The root spans goodness and excellence and the act of selecting what is best from among alternatives.
body.text_en: Khiyar comes from the root meaning 'to be good,' and by extension 'to choose the better.' In the marketplace it names a contracting party's option to confirm or cancel a sale — literally the right to pick the better outcome.

lexicon.lane_en: 1 عَلِقَ بِهِ ذ , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, TA,) aor. عَلَقَ , (Msb,) inf. n. عَلَقٌ (S, O, Msb, KL, TA) and عَلقَةٌ (L, TA) [and app. عُلُوقٌ also, as will be seen from what follows]; and , (S, MA, Mgh, O, Msb,) and ; (O, Msb, KL;) It hung to it; it was, or became, suspended to it: (so the first and last accord.

body.meaning_en: to cling, hang, be attached
body.morphology: A noun formed from the root, naming the clinging thing — the blood-like clot that hangs onto the wall of the womb.
body.semantic_field: The root spans clinging, suspension, and attachment, both physical (a leech gripping) and figurative (being emotionally attached).
body.text_en: Alaqah is built from a root whose core sense is 'to cling or hang.' It names the early embryonic stage — a clot that clings to the womb — because the word pictures something gripping and suspended, exactly as a leech attaches to the skin.

derivatives.meaning_en: a chewed lump; the embryonic flesh stage

lexicon.lane_en: مُضْغَةٌ ذ A piece, or bit, of flesh (T, S, K), &c.: (T, K:) or a morsel, or gobbet, of flesh, i. e. a piece of flesh such as a man puts into his mouth: (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA:) or as much as is chewed [ at once ]: (Msb:) and such as the heart, and the tongue, of a man: (TA:) and a fœtus when it has become like a lump of flesh: see Kur. xxii. 5; and see خَلِيقٌ .

body.meaning_en: to chew
body.morphology: A noun of small portion from the root, naming a morsel — a lump of flesh the size of what is chewed at once.
body.semantic_field: The root spans chewing and mastication, and by extension a bite-sized lump of flesh.
body.text_en: Mudghah is drawn from the root 'to chew.' It names the embryonic stage that resembles a chewed lump of flesh — a morsel the size of what the mouth works at one time.

body.meaning_en: to work, act, do a deed
body.morphology: A verbal noun from amila ("to act"), meaning a deed, work, or action.
body.semantic_field: The root spans labor, action, and agency — the doing of a deed as opposed to mere belief or word.
body.text_en: Amal is the ordinary word for a deed or work, from a root meaning simply to act. It marks the domain of what a person does, distinct from what they merely know or profess.

derivatives.meaning_en: one who leads, stands in front

body.meaning_en: to aim toward, to head for a source
body.morphology: A noun of the pattern fuʿla from the root, denoting a body of people gathered around and aiming toward one thing.
body.semantic_field: The root spans intending/heading toward, an origin or mother-source, and leadership at the front that others orient to.
body.text_en: Umma comes from a root meaning to aim toward and to head for a source — the same root that gives umm (mother) and imam (the one at the front). An umma is thus a community bound together by facing one direction: a people gathered around a shared source and aim.

body.meaning_en: to be secure, safe; to trust
body.morphology: A form-IV verbal noun of amana ('to believe'), built on amina ('to be secure'), so faith is entering a state of trust and security.
body.semantic_field: runs from safety and security to trust, fidelity and the giving and keeping of a trust.
body.text_en: The root '-m-n is the vocabulary of security and trust, giving both amn (safety) and amaana (a trust one is bound to keep). Iman, faith, is the form-IV act built on it — placing oneself in a state of secure trust — and the one who does so is a mu'min.

lexicon.lane_en: ٱمْرَأٌ ذ and ٱمْرَأَةٌ &c: see مَرْءٌ .

body.meaning_en: manhood, being a man
body.morphology: a verbal noun (maṣdar) naming the abstract quality of manliness, formed from mar' ('a man')
body.semantic_field: spans manhood, human dignity, and the chivalric ideal of upright, honourable conduct
body.text_en: Muruwwa comes from the root meaning 'a man,' the same root that gives mar' (a man) and imra'a (a woman). It names the whole ideal of manly virtue — dignity, honour, and upright conduct — treating true manliness as a moral quality rather than merely being male.

lexicon.lane_en: 1 نَفَقَتِ السُّوقُ ذ The marked became brisk, its goods selling much; syn. قَامَت . (K.) -b2- نَفَقَ It was, or became, saleable; easy, or ready, of sale; or in much demand: see its syn. رَاجَ . -b3- نَفَقَتْ It (a commodity, سِلْعَة ,) was in much demand: and she (a woman) was demanded in marriage by many. (Msb.) -b4- نَفِقَتِ الدَّراَهِمُ , inf. n. نَفَقٌ , The dirhems passed away, came to an end, or became spent or exhausted; syn. نَفِدَت . (Msb.)

body.meaning_en: to spend, disburse; to be used up
body.morphology: A verbal noun from the root, naming the expenditure — specifically the maintenance one is obliged to provide.
body.semantic_field: The root spans spending and outlay, and — through the tunnel-image of nifaq — the two-facedness of the hypocrite who shows one thing and hides another.
body.text_en: Nafaqah comes from the root 'to spend.' As a legal term it is the obligatory maintenance a person must disburse — for a spouse or dependent — the outlay that keeps a household provided for.

body.meaning_en: to breathe
body.morphology: A noun naming the breathing self — the living soul or ego.
body.semantic_field: Spans breath, life, self, and the appetitive ego that must be disciplined.
body.text_en: The root means to breathe, and from breath comes nafs, the breathing self. In spiritual writing the nafs is the lower self or ego whose cravings the seeker struggles to master.

lexicon.lane_en: 1 نَشَزٌ ذ , aor. نَشُزَ and نَشِزَ , (S, Msb, K,) inf. n. نَشْزٌ , (S, K,) or نُشُوزٌ , (Msb,) He rose, or raised himself, (S, A, Msb, K,) فِى المَكَانِ in the place, (S,) and فِى مَجْلِسِهِ in his sitting-place, (TA,) and عَنْ مَكَانِهِ , (A,) or مِنْ مَكَانِهِ , (Msb,) from his place: (A, Msb:) or he rose a little in his sittingplace: (TA:) or he stood up after sitting.

body.meaning_en: to rise up, stand out
body.morphology: a verbal noun (maṣdar) of the pattern فُعُول from nashaza, 'to rise from one's place'
body.semantic_field: rising ground, elevation, standing up, and by extension rebellion against a rightful claim
body.text_en: The root n-sh-z means to rise or raise oneself above a place, as high ground rises above a plain. Nushūz is the verbal noun, applied in marital law to one spouse rising against and away from the other's rightful due.

body.meaning_en: to speak, articulate, utter
body.morphology: An active participle of nataqa, 'to speak', so a natiq is 'the speaker' — the prophet who articulates an outward revealed law.
body.semantic_field: spans articulate speech and, by extension, reasoned utterance and logic.
body.text_en: The root n-t-q means to speak and articulate, and it also underlies mantiq, logic, as reasoned speech. A natiq is 'the speaker' — the prophet who voices the outward law, standing opposite the silent one who keeps its inner sense.

derivatives.meaning_en: an outing into open, distant space

body.meaning_en: to be far from, free of, pure
body.morphology: A form-II verbal noun of nazzaha, the act of declaring something free of every defect.
body.semantic_field: The root spans purity, remoteness from blemish, and being held far above imperfection.
body.text_en: Tanzih means declaring God utterly free of any likeness or defect, from a root whose sense is being far removed and pure. It is the argument that God stands above every image or attribute the mind might try to attach to Him.

derivatives.meaning_en: to knit the brow, draw the face together

body.meaning_en: to gather, pivot, form an axis
body.morphology: a noun naming the fixed pivot-pin of a millstone, hence any axis or chief point around which things turn
body.semantic_field: the root spans gathering/drawing together, the pivot of a turning thing, and the fixed center or chief
body.text_en: The root q-ṭ-b names the fixed pin at the center of a millstone around which the whole stone turns. A quṭb is therefore any pivot or axis, and figuratively the central figure on whom an entire order depends — as when the imamate is called the 'pole' of religion.

lexicon.lane_en: 4 أَقْبَلْتُهُ الشَّىْءَ ذ I made it to face the thing: (S, K:) and الشَّىْءَ app. signifies the same: see a verse of El-Aashà voce اِرْتِسَامٌ . -b2- أَقْبَلَ بِهِ [ He turned it forward; contr. of أَدْبَرَ بِهِ ].

body.meaning_en: to face, come toward, receive/accept
body.morphology: a noun of the fiʿlah pattern denoting the direction one faces (qiblah), from the sense of turning toward and confronting
body.semantic_field: the root spans facing, fronting, coming forward, acceptance, and what lies 'before' in place or time
body.text_en: The root q-b-l is about facing and coming toward something. The qibla is the fixed direction the worshipper turns to face, and the same root of turning-toward also yields acceptance (taqabbala) and 'before' (qabl).

lexicon.lane_en: 1 قَدَرْتُ الشَّىْءَ ذ , aor. قَدِرَ and قَدُرَ , [or the former only accord. to the Mgh., as will be seen by what follows,] inf. n. قَدْرٌ , (S, Msb,) is from التَّقْدِيرُ , (S,) [or] it signifies the same as الشَّىْءَ , inf.

body.meaning_en: to measure, apportion, determine; to have power
body.morphology: qadar is a noun meaning the measure or determined portion God apportions to each thing, and by extension His decree.
body.semantic_field: spans measuring out an amount, fixing a due proportion, and the power to determine.
body.text_en: The root ق-د-ر is about measuring a thing out to its exact due amount, and the power such measuring implies. Qadar is God's measuring-out of all things — the fixed proportion decreed for each, paired in theology with qada, the decree that puts it into effect.

derivatives.meaning_en: a case or matter to be decided

body.meaning_en: to decree, decide, settle, bring to completion
body.morphology: qaḍāʾ is the verbal noun of qaḍā, the decisive settling or judgment by which a matter is concluded and executed.
body.semantic_field: spans deciding a case, finishing a task, and carrying a decree through to its end.
body.text_en: The root ق-ض-ي is the act of settling a thing once and for all — a judge deciding a case, a task carried through to its finish. Qada is God's decisive decree, the sentence handed down and executed, paired in theology with qadar, the measuring that precedes it.

derivatives.meaning_en: a tether that binds a camel

body.meaning_en: to bind, to restrain, to comprehend
body.morphology: verbal noun of ʿaqala, 'he bound / grasped with the mind'
body.semantic_field: runs from tethering an animal to restraining oneself to grasping a meaning
body.text_en: The root ع-ق-ل first means to tie down — the same word names the rope that tethers a camel — and from that comes the mind that binds and holds meaning fast. Aql is this intellect, which for Ali is a restraining, unifying faculty far deeper than ordinary reasoning.

body.meaning_en: to be strong, powerful
body.morphology: A noun of the pattern fuʿla from the verb qawiya, naming strength itself or a faculty/capacity possessed of strength.
body.semantic_field: The root spans physical strength, potency, and the inner faculty or capacity by which a being is able to act.
body.text_en: Quwwa comes from a root meaning to be strong, and it names strength or power in the abstract. In technical usage it also denotes a faculty — an inner capacity or potency by which a person is able to do something.

derivatives.meaning_en: what is known / recognized as right

body.meaning_en: to know, to recognize, to be acquainted with
body.morphology: verbal noun of ʿarafa, 'he knew / recognized'; denotes knowledge by acquaintance
body.semantic_field: spans recognition, acquaintance, and knowledge won through direct experience
body.text_en: The root ع-ر-ف is knowing by recognition — meeting something and knowing it firsthand, not merely knowing about it. Marifa is this experiential knowledge of God, the gnosis of the one who has come to recognize Him rather than only reason toward Him.

body.meaning_en: to see, to perceive
body.morphology: A form III verbal noun (mura'ah) meaning to act so as to be seen by others.
body.semantic_field: Spans sight, perception, opinion, and appearance before the eyes of others.
body.text_en: The root means to see. Riya is worship performed to be seen — good deeds done for the eyes of people rather than for God, the exact opposite of sincerity.

derivatives.meaning_en: a street or thoroughfare; the Lawgiver
legislation, the act of enacting law

body.meaning_en: to open a road, to mark out a path to water
body.morphology: A noun on the fa'ilah pattern naming the path itself, originally the track leading down to a watering place.
body.semantic_field: Spans opening, road-making, and legislating a clear way for people to follow.
body.text_en: The root means to open up a path, especially the trodden way down to water. Shari'ah is that opened road turned into a metaphor: the clear way of life God marks out, as vital to the soul as water is to the thirsty.

derivatives.meaning_en: one who ascribes partners to God

lexicon.lane_en: شِرْكٌ ذ is an inf. n. of شَرِكَهُ , as mentioned in the first sentence of this art.: (Mgh, Msb:) or a subst. therefrom: (S:) and is syn. with , [signifying A sharing, participating or participation, partaking, or copartnership, and mentioned before as an inf.

body.meaning_en: to share, associate, be a partner
body.morphology: shirk is a verbal noun meaning the act of making a partner — in religion, associating another with God.
body.semantic_field: spans sharing, partnership, and holding a thing in common with another.
body.text_en: The root ش-ر-ك is plain partnership, two parties sharing in one thing as associates. Shirk is that idea turned against tawhid: setting up a partner alongside God, the one sin the creed of oneness exists to exclude.

derivatives.meaning_en: one who associates partners with God

lexicon.lane_en: شِرْكٌ ذ is an inf. n. of شَرِكَهُ , as mentioned in the first sentence of this art.: (Mgh, Msb:) or a subst. therefrom: (S:) and is syn. with , [signifying A sharing, participating or participation, partaking, or copartnership, and mentioned before as an inf.

body.meaning_en: to share, to associate as a partner
body.morphology: verbal noun of sharika, 'he shared / became a partner'
body.semantic_field: spans sharing, partnership, and association of one thing with another
body.text_en: The root ش-ر-ك is the ordinary word for sharing or taking a business partner. Shirk turns that neutral idea into the gravest error — assigning God a partner, sharing with something else the devotion owed to Him alone.

lexicon.lane_en: شَيْطَانٌ ذ a word of well-known meaning [i. e. A devil; and with the article ال , the devil, Satan ]: (S, K:) any that is excessively, or inordinately, proud or corrupt or unbelieving or rebellious, or that is insolent and audacious in pride and in acts of rebellion, of mankind, and of the jinn, or genii, and of beasts; (A'Obeyd, S, Msb, K;) as is shown in relation to the first and second of these by what is said in the Kur vi.

body.meaning_en: to be remote, far off (from truth or mercy)
body.morphology: A noun from shatana, 'to be far/remote', naming a being that is distant from good — a devil, of humankind or of the jinn.
body.semantic_field: turns on remoteness and contrariness — distance from goodness expressed as rebellious opposition.
body.text_en: The root sh-t-n means to be far and remote, and a shaytan is one who is distant from truth and mercy — a devil, whether among people or jinn. The classical lexica extend the word to anyone excessively proud or rebellious, so it names a type of contrariness, not only a single figure.

derivatives.meaning_en: old age, the state of being elderly
a council of elders; the office of a shaykh

body.meaning_en: to grow old, to become an elder
body.morphology: A noun of the sound triliteral, naming the aged one and by extension the senior authority who has matured in knowledge.
body.semantic_field: Spans age, seniority, and the authority that accrues from long experience.
body.text_en: The root means to grow old and become an elder. From it comes shaykh, which starts as 'old man' and grows into 'master' — the one whose years have ripened into authority worth following.

body.meaning_en: to be safe, whole, sound; peace
body.morphology: A verbal noun of the form-IV verb aslama, 'to surrender oneself wholly', so islam is literally the act of handing oneself over into safety.
body.semantic_field: spans safety, soundness and freedom from defect on one side and peace, reconciliation and submission on the other.
body.text_en: Islam comes from the root s-l-m, whose core sense is to be safe, sound and whole, from which grows the idea of peace. The word itself is the act of aslama — surrendering oneself entirely — so a muslim is one who enters that safety by handing himself over.

derivatives.meaning_en: to betake oneself to, to aim toward

body.meaning_en: to resort to; to be eternal, self-sufficient
body.morphology: An abstract noun (-iyyah) formed from the divine name al-Samad, "the Eternal, Self-Sufficient" (Quran 112:2).
body.semantic_field: The root spans being the one all turn to for need, and being everlasting, whole, and dependent on nothing.
body.text_en: Samadiyyah is the abstract quality of being al-Samad, the one to whom all creatures turn while He needs nothing in return. It names the mode of divine self-sufficiency and everlastingness, drawn from a root about being the sole recourse.

body.meaning_en: to be silent, still
body.morphology: An active participle of samata ('to keep silent'), so a samit is 'the silent one' — the figure who holds the inner meaning without proclaiming it.
body.semantic_field: is confined to silence, stillness and the withholding of speech.
body.text_en: The root s-m-t means to be silent and still. A samit is 'the silent one' — in this book the foundation-figure who guards the hidden meaning quietly, paired against the natiq, the speaker who proclaims the outward law.

derivatives.meaning_en: one who does good / acts beautifully

lexicon.lane_en: حَسَنٌ حسن حسنن Having, or possessing, the quality termed حُسْنٌ [which see above; good, or goodly, (generally the latter,) beautiful, comely, pleasing or pleasant, &c.]; (Msb, K, TA;) either intrinsically, as when applied to belief in God and in his attributes; or extrinsically, as when applied to war against unbelievers, for this is not good in itself: said to be the only epithet of its measure except بَطَلٌ : (TA:) and signifies the same, (IB, K,) because from حَسُنَ , like عَظِيمٌ and كَريِمٌ from عَظُمَ and كَرُمَ , (IB, TA,) and , (K,) but this is an intensive epithet, [signifying very …

body.meaning_en: to be good, beautiful, excellent
body.morphology: verbal noun of the form-IV verb aḥsana, 'he did well / acted beautifully'
body.semantic_field: joins the moral good to the beautiful and the excellent
body.text_en: In the root ح-س-ن goodness and beauty are the same word, so to do well is to make something beautiful. Ihsan is the highest of these forms: to worship and act as though seeing God, giving every deed its full inward beauty.

derivatives.meaning_en: to enact, to prescribe a practice

body.meaning_en: to set a course, to establish a way; to sharpen
body.morphology: A noun on the fu'lah pattern naming an established, well-worn way of doing a thing.
body.semantic_field: Spans setting precedent, smoothing a path, and sharpening/shaping into form.
body.text_en: The root means to lay down and smooth a well-trodden course. The Sunnah is the established way of the Prophet — the path he set that others now follow.

body.meaning_en: to found, lay a base
body.morphology: A noun from assa/assasa meaning the foundation on which a structure is raised, used here for the figure who holds the hidden base beneath a prophet's law.
body.semantic_field: concentrates on foundation, groundwork and the establishing base underneath what is built.
body.text_en: The root '-s-s is the vocabulary of foundations — the base laid before anything is built upon it. An asas is thus a 'foundation' figure who carries the hidden groundwork beneath the outward law a prophet brings.

body.meaning_en: to be firm, fixed, steadfast
body.morphology: the verbal noun of the form-IV verb athbata, 'to make firm / establish', hence affirmation or proof
body.semantic_field: the root spans firmness, stability, steadfastness, and establishing something as certain
body.text_en: The root th-b-t is about firmness and standing fast. Ithbāt is the act of making something firmly established — affirming or proving it — which is why a treatise on 'affirming the imamate' rests on this root.

body.meaning_en: to be one, single, unique
body.morphology: verbal noun of the form-II verb waḥḥada, 'he declared / affirmed to be one'
body.semantic_field: spans oneness, singularity, uniqueness, and unification
body.text_en: The root و-ح-د names oneness in its strongest form — not merely one among a series, but a uniqueness nothing shares. Tawhid is the active affirmation of that oneness, the declaration at the heart of Islamic belief that God alone is truly One.

body.meaning_en: to agree, to be in harmony, to suit
body.morphology: A form II verbal noun (tawfiq) meaning the act of bringing things into accord and enabling them to fit together.
body.semantic_field: Spans agreement, concord, and the fitting-together of means toward a good end.
body.text_en: The root means to fit together in agreement. Tawfiq is God's aligning of a person's will and circumstances so that they succeed — the divine enabling of a good act.

body.meaning_en: to be one, single, unique; to unify
body.morphology: A form-II verbal noun of wahhada, literally the act of "making one" or declaring one.
body.semantic_field: The root spans oneness, singularity, and the act of unifying — being alone without a second.
body.text_en: Tawhid is built from the root meaning "to be one," and as a form-II noun it names the deliberate act of declaring God one. It is not merely counting God as a single item but affirming a oneness that admits no partner, division, or second.

derivatives.meaning_en: delegation, granting of power of attorney

body.meaning_en: to entrust, to appoint an agent
body.morphology: A form V verbal noun (tawakkul) meaning to entrust one's affair completely to another.
body.semantic_field: Spans entrusting, delegating, and appointing someone to act on one's behalf.
body.text_en: The root means to entrust your affair to an agent who acts for you. Tawakkul is doing exactly that with God — handing the outcome over to Him after doing your part.

derivatives.meaning_en: the outcome to which a thing returns
a returning, a reverting to origin

body.meaning_en: to return to the origin, to revert
body.morphology: taʾwīl is the verbal noun of the form-II verb awwala, 'to trace a thing back to its first meaning' — carrying an outward text back to its inner origin.
body.semantic_field: spans returning, tracing back to a beginning, and the outcome to which a thing finally comes.
body.text_en: The root أ-و-ل is the idea of going back to a first thing, the origin from which something came and to which it returns. Tawil is interpretation of exactly this kind — carrying the outward words of a text back to the inner, original meaning they point to.

body.meaning_en: to be near; to be a friend, guardian, in charge
body.morphology: A verbal noun from waliya, meaning guardianship, authority, allegiance, or sainthood.
body.semantic_field: The root spans nearness, friendship, protection, and rightful authority — the bond between a protector and those in his charge.
body.text_en: Wilayah comes from a root joining the ideas of nearness, friendship, and being in charge, so it can mean guardianship, authority, or devoted allegiance. In the book it names the binding loyalty owed to the Imams and Friends of God as a matter of teaching.

body.meaning_en: to enjoin, charge, bequeath, appoint
body.morphology: waṣī is the active participle, 'the one charged and appointed' — the designated legatee entrusted with a trust and succession.
body.semantic_field: spans enjoining a duty, making a bequest, and appointing an executor to carry it out.
body.text_en: The root و-ص-ي is about entrusting a charge, laying a binding injunction on someone or bequeathing something to be carried out. A wasi is the one so entrusted — the appointed legatee who inherits the trust and continues the work of the one who named him.

body.meaning_en: to grow, purify, be pure
body.morphology: a verbal noun (zakāh) naming the purifying almsgiving that makes wealth grow and clean
body.semantic_field: the root spans growth, increase, purity, and moral wholesomeness
body.text_en: The root z-k-w joins two ideas that are one in the Arabic mind: growth and purity, for what is cleansed also thrives. Zakat is the obligatory alms that purifies the giver's wealth and soul while causing what remains to grow.
